standard_prerequisites.name: The module pushed forward along a closed immersion has the same stalk over the base
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, the remark at proof line 3534, using the identification of the stalks
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the pushforward of the module to the affine space is still flat over the base at the image point, which is the hypothesis needed to apply the finite presentation statement there.

core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case and embed into an affine space: the problem is local on the source and the base, so assume both affine and choose a surjection from a polynomial algebra onto the coordinate ring of the source, i.e. a closed immersion of the source into an affine space over the base (proof lines 3525-3533).

Apply the finite presentation statement upstairs: let t be the image point and push the module forward along the closed immersion; the stalk of the pushforward at t is isomorphic to the stalk of the module at x as modules over the local ring of the base, so the pushforward is flat over the base at t, and the finite presentation statement applies to the projection from the affine space (proof lines 3534-3539).

Cut back down: from the resulting elementary etale neighbourhood, affine etale neighbourhood over the base and freeness of the global sections of the pulled back pushforward, take the fibre product of that neighbourhood with the source over the affine space, which is a closed subscheme of it and gives the required solution for the original morphism (proof lines 3540-3553).
proof_roadmap: Go affine and embed the source into an affine space over the base (proof lines 3525-3533).
Apply the finite presentation statement to the pushforward along the closed immersion (proof lines 3534-3539).
Cut the resulting neighbourhood back down along the fibre product (proof lines 3540-3553).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the finite type variant of the pointwise freeness statement: for a locally finite type morphism and a finite type module flat at a point, after an elementary etale neighbourhood of the image there is an affine etale neighbourhood of the point, with the same residue field, on which the global sections of the pulled back module are free (statement lines 3500-3523, tag 05KZ). The proof is a genuine reduction: it embeds the source into an affine space over the base, applies the finite presentation statement to the pushforward of the module along that closed immersion (whose stalk is unchanged over the base so that flatness persists), and then cuts the resulting neighbourhood back down by a fibre product. The reduction through the affine space is the substance, so the claim is H2.
